learning_objectives: Explain reading for meaning using simple language and an example.
Explain sequence and inference using simple language and an example.
Explain vocabulary in context using simple language and an example.
Explain moral/idea and evidence using simple language and an example.
Apply the chapter ideas independently in an unfamiliar but age-appropriate situation.

concept_map.mastery_evidence: Learner explains and applies reading for meaning.
Learner explains and applies sequence and inference.

lessons.objective: Learner can understand, explain and apply reading for meaning.
teaching_sequence: Begin with an original short example connected to the learner's life.
Ask what the learner notices before giving formal explanation.
Model how to use textual clues or context.
Guide one response, then remove support.
Ask for an original example or retelling.
lessons.checkpoint: Explain reading for meaning without notes and solve a new example.

flashcards.back: Define reading for meaning, give an example, and explain why it matters.
Define sequence and inference, give an example, and explain why it matters.
Define vocabulary in context, give an example, and explain why it matters.
Define moral/idea and evidence, give an example, and explain why it matters.

interactive_activities.title: Explore reading for meaning
interactive_activities.instructions: Use a safe, age-appropriate task specifically focused on reading for meaning. Record what you notice, explain it, and state what you learned.

interactive_activities.title: Use it in a new situation
interactive_activities.instructions: Create a new situation where sequence and inference is useful and explain your reasoning.

interactive_activities.title: Teach it back
interactive_activities.instructions: Teach moral/idea and evidence to a beginner in 3–5 clear steps.
